interface.longDescription:
Dillie is a team collaboration workspace that brings messaging, projects, calendar, meetings, mail and files together in one place. The Dillie app for ChatGPT connects ChatGPT to the projects and tasks in your Dillie workspace, so you can check on work and keep it moving without leaving the conversation.

Ask in plain language and ChatGPT works with your real project data:

- "Show my Dillie projects" lists every project you belong to.
- "How far along is the website redesign?" returns task counts by status and overall progress for that project.
- "What is assigned to me?" filters tasks by assignee, status or any other field you track.
- "Open the onboarding task" shows the task, its full description and its sub-task tree.
- "Add a task to prepare the release notes, due Friday" creates the task in the right project.
- "Mark it done with a short note" completes it and records the note in the task's conversation.

Sprint planning is covered too: create a sprint, start it, assign tasks to it and complete it when the work is done. You can also create a new project, update task fields, rewrite a task description in Markdown, or cancel a task — and undo a completion or cancellation if you change your mind. Questions about how Dillie itself works are answered from Dillie's public product documentation.

Results come back as structured data, so ChatGPT can summarize a project at a glance, group tasks the way you ask and carry a project or task from one answer into your next request.

How it works with your account

- You sign in with your own Dillie account through Dillie's standard OAuth sign-in. ChatGPT never sees your password.
- The app can only see and change what your Dillie account can see and change. Workspace and project permissions in Dillie still apply to every request.
- The app asks for access to your basic profile (name and email), and to read and write projects and tasks. It does not read your messages, mail, files or calendar.
- Actions that change your data — creating, updating, completing or cancelling — are declared to ChatGPT as write actions. The app has no delete actions.
- You can see and disconnect ChatGPT at any time from Settings > Connected apps in Dillie.

Requirements

A Dillie account and membership in at least one workspace. New to Dillie? Create a workspace at https://dillie.work and invite your team.

Support: https://dillie.work/support
capabilities: Browse your Dillie projects with details, members and custom fields
See project statistics: task counts by status and overall progress
Filter and sort tasks by assignee, status or any other field
Open a task with its full description and its sub-task tree
Create tasks and sub-tasks with title, assignee, due date and other fields
Update task fields and rewrite task descriptions in Markdown
Complete or cancel tasks with an optional note, and undo either
Plan sprints: create, start and complete them, and assign tasks to a sprint
Create a new project in your workspace
Search and read the public Dillie product documentation
defaultPrompt: Show my Dillie projects and how far along each one is
What tasks are assigned to me in Dillie this week?
Create a Dillie task to prepare the release notes, due Friday

positive.description: List the projects the signed-in user belongs to
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the projects the user belongs to, with their names. Makes no changes.

positive.description: Summarize the progress of one project
positive.prompt: How far along is the Website Redesign project in Dillie?
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes that project's task counts by status and its overall progress.

positive.description: List the tasks assigned to the signed-in user in one project
positive.prompt: What tasks are assigned to me in Website Redesign?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists only the tasks assigned to the signed-in user.

positive.description: Create a task with a title and a due date
positive.prompt: Create a task "Prepare release notes" in Website Redesign, due next Friday
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a task with the given title and due date and reports its issue key.

positive.description: Complete a task with a note
positive.prompt: Mark the task "Prepare release notes" as done with the note "Shipped in v1.2"
positive.expected_behavior: Marks the task as done and records the note in the task's conversation.

negative.description: Unrelated to Dillie, so no Dillie tool should be called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Seoul tomorrow?

negative.description: The app has no delete tools, so no write tool should be called; the user should be told to delete the project in Dillie.
negative.prompt: Delete the Website Redesign project in Dillie

negative.description: Sending messages is outside this app's scope (projects and tasks only), so no tool should be called and the user should be told the feature is not supported.
negative.prompt: Send a message to my team channel in Dillie saying I'm running late

publication.release_notes: First release. Browse your projects and project statistics; filter, create, update, complete and cancel tasks; plan sprints; and read Dillie's public documentation — all from ChatGPT. Sign in with your Dillie account; your existing workspace and project permissions apply.
